question: What are the two primary functions of the human nose?
explanation: The nose primarily functions as an airway for breathing (respiration) and as the sensory organ for smell (olfaction). [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is it important for the nose to condition inspired air before it reaches the lungs?

options.A: To increase the total volume of air the lungs can hold
options.B: To protect delicate lower airway tissues from damage
options.C: To speed up the rate of gas exchange in the alveoli
options.D: To remove all carbon dioxide from the incoming atmosphere

explanation: Warming, humidifying, and filtering incoming air prevents cold, dry, and dirty air from irritating or damaging the sensitive tissues of the trachea and lungs. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h1)

question: What structures divide the internal nasal cavity into left and right halves?
explanation: The nasal septum sits right down the middle, separating the left and right nasal cavities from each other. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of the nasal conchae or turbinates on the lateral wall?

options.A: To trap large dust particles directly at the external nares
options.B: To produce tears that lubricate the nasal mucosa
options.C: To create turbulent airflow and increase surface area
options.D: To house the specialized receptors for the sense of taste

explanation: The curvy shape of the conchae forces air to swirl around, maximizing contact with the warm, moist lining so it gets conditioned properly. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h2)

question: What type of lining tissue covers the inside of the respiratory tract?
explanation: Even though the medical name sounds like a tongue-twister, you'll see it everywhere in nursing! This special tissue has tiny hair-like cilia that sweep dirt and germs right out of your airways. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main role of the mucociliary escalator in the nasal cavity?

options.A: To secrete specialized enzymes that dissolve food odors
options.B: To pump fresh oxygen directly into the pulmonary capillaries
options.C: To cool down overheated air before it enters the trachea
options.D: To transport trapped debris toward the throat for removal

explanation: Beating cilia move the sticky mucus layer backward so dust and bacteria are safely swallowed rather than entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the paired paranasal sinuses?
explanation: The temporal bone does not contain a paranasal sinus; the four paired sinuses are maxillary, frontal, sphenoid, and ethmoid. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why do people with common colds frequently develop sinus headaches and pressure?

options.A: The brain increases blood flow to the sinuses to fight off the virus
options.B: Cold air freezes the fluid inside the sphenoid and frontal cavities
options.C: Swollen nasal linings block the tiny drainage openings of the sinuses
options.D: Excess mucus production physically shatters the underlying skull bones

explanation: When swelling closes off the narrow ostia, mucus gets trapped inside the sinus cavities, causing pressure to build up and trigger pain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h4)

question: What are the coarse hairs located inside the nasal vestibule called?
explanation: Vibrissae are the stiff, coarse hairs at the entrance of the nose that catch large bugs, dust, and debris. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does the nasal cavity manage to warm up cold inspired air so effectively?

options.A: Friction from the turbinates generates constant physical heat
options.B: A rich network of blood vessels in the submucosa transfers body heat
options.C: Inhaled oxygen undergoes rapid chemical combustion inside the meatus
options.D: Specialized sweat glands inside the nostrils pump thermal energy

explanation: The lamina propria contains a massive supply of blood vessels that radiate heat, warming the air as it swirls past. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which cranial nerve transmits sensory signals for the sense of smell from the nose to the brain?
explanation: Cranial nerve I, the olfactory nerve, carries smell sensations straight from the nasal roof into the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h6)

question: Through which bony structure do olfactory nerve fibers pass to reach the brain's olfactory bulb?

options.A: Squamous part of the temporal bone
options.B: Cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone

explanation: Olfactory nerve bundles pass upward through the tiny perforations of the cribriform plate to reach the olfactory bulbs inside the cranium. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the common medical term for a nosebleed originating from the anterior nasal septum?
explanation: Epistaxis is the clinical term for bleeding from the blood vessels inside the nasal cavity. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h7)

question: A patient is brought to the clinic after a motorcycle crash, and clear fluid is dripping from one nostril. What serious injury should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Severe allergic reaction to helmet padding
options.B: Fracture of the cribriform plate with CSF leak
options.C: Rupture of the maxillary paranasal sinus

explanation: Clear fluid coming from the nose after a head impact is a major red flag. It usually means a skull fracture has torn the lining near the brain, letting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak out. Always report this immediately! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h7)
